parts.note: Right body and channels/stages, but it missed the key statutory 6-month-from-awareness/12-month cap time limit.
Right ombudsman, but it only reached the checker, not the live SPSO form page, and missed the outage/9-month delay and some scope limits.
It omitted the compensation route entirely: no NHS redress, only a civil negligence claim with a 3-year limitation.
Good catch that Scottish legal aid is available for medical negligence, but it missed the main tests, QOCS and capped success-fee details.
It gave no route to actually find a claimant medical-negligence solicitor or the SLAB/Law Society tools.
Right Scottish guidance body, but it missed the key nuance that there is no SIGN scaphoid guideline and NICE NG38 is the practical reference.
PASS is the right independent support service, though direct PASS contact details and scope were thin.
Records route was essentially correct: portal needs login, and the SAR form can be sent by email or post.

smart: It correctly recognised a major Scotland-specific point many agents miss: civil legal aid is available for medical negligence in Scotland.
worst: It missed the compensation route altogether, including that there is no NHS redress scheme and the only route is a civil claim subject to the Scottish 3-year limitation.
